references.text: Describes Israel's victory over the Amorite king Sihon and King Og of Bashan, which are the same events Joshua refers to in his speech.
Moses tells how God gave the Amorites into Israel's hands and let them conquer their land on the east side of the Jordan.
The continuation of Israel's conquest of the areas east of the Jordan, including the victory over King Og of Bashan.
Rahab mentions that the people of Jericho had heard how God destroyed the two Amorite kings Sihon and Og on the east side of the Jordan.
The Gibeonites refer to what the Lord did with the two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan.
Jephthah refers to Israel's victory over the Amorites and how they took their land as possession.
The psalm praises God for striking down great nations and giving their land as an inheritance to Israel, including Sihon and Og.
Praise to God who struck down great kings and gave their land as an inheritance, specifically mentioning Sihon and Og.
Amos reminds Israel that it was God who destroyed the Amorites before them, even though the Amorites were powerful.
Nehemiah recalls how God gave the Israelites kingdoms and peoples, and let them conquer the land of Sihon and Og.
